title: Reading a Berghaus Label Before You Buy: Jackets, Fleeces and Packs for Kenyan Trails
meta_title: Berghaus in Kenya: 3 Reliable Picks for Rain and Cold
meta_description: Berghaus in Kenya: Hydroshell vs Gore-Tex jackets, Prism fleeces, Freeflow packs, sizing, second-hand checks and where to find Berghaus in Nairobi.
excerpt: Berghaus makes Gore-Tex and Hydroshell jackets, Polartec fleeces and Freeflow daypacks. Here is which labels suit Kenyan trails, how British sizing runs and what to check when buying Berghaus second-hand in Nairobi.

content:
Berghaus is a British outdoor brand, and in Kenya it is best known for waterproof jackets, Polartec fleeces and ventilated daypacks. For Kenyan hikers, a Berghaus Gore-Tex or Hydroshell shell suits the long and short rains, the Aberdares and Mt Kenya's moorland, while older AQ jackets are fine for wet day hikes near Nairobi.

Most Berghaus gear in Nairobi arrives second-hand, so you rarely get a shop assistant explaining the swing tag. Below we decode the labels you will see, match each product line to real Kenyan trails, explain how British sizing runs, list what to check on a used piece, and show where to look for Berghaus in Nairobi.

Berghaus in Brief

  • Origin: Founded in 1966 in Newcastle upon Tyne, England, by climbers Peter Lockey and Gordon Davison.
  • Name: German for "mountain house", a loose translation of their first shop, the LD Mountain Centre.
  • Waterproof labels: Gore-Tex at the top, Berghaus's own Hydroshell in the middle, AQ and AQ2 on budget and older jackets.
  • Best Kenyan use: Rainy-season day hikes, the Aberdares, Mt Kenya and Kilimanjaro.
  • Sizing: British cut; spec sheets list back length, e.g. 79 cm on a size L RG Alpha 2.0 jacket.
  • Buying in Nairobi: Mostly thrifted; big-brand stock at our Mountain Mall shop changes week to week.

What Is Berghaus Known For?

Berghaus is known for waterproof shells, fleeces and rucksacks designed for wet British hills. The brand also makes insulated jackets, base layers, trousers, gaiters and walking boots, so a hiker can dress head to toe in it.

The story starts in 1966, when Peter Lockey and Gordon Davison opened the LD Mountain Centre in Newcastle, a specialist climbing shop. Other retailers were slow to stock products from a rival shop, so the pair put their own designs under a new name, Berghaus, which hinted at German engineering. By 1972 the company was making its own kit, including the Cyclops rucksack, often described as one of the first packs with an internal frame.

A few firsts still shape what you find on a Nairobi rail today. Berghaus was among the earliest European brands to use Gore-Tex, from 1977. Its Yeti gaiter, launched in 1979, had a rubber rand first cut from old tractor inner tubes, and the gaiter is still used on expeditions. In the 1980s it introduced zip-in fleece jackets and the Extrem range for serious mountaineering. Since 1993 Berghaus has belonged to Pentland Group, which also owns Speedo, and its head office is in Sunderland.

Why should that matter to a hiker in Kenya? Because gear built for Scotland's Cairngorms and England's Lake District handles cold fog, sideways drizzle and wind, and that is exactly what you meet above about 2,500 m on our mountains. You can read the founders' own account on the Berghaus website.

Which Berghaus Waterproof Label Do You Need for Kenyan Rain?

Pick a Berghaus Gore-Tex or Hydroshell Elite jacket for full-day rain and high mountains, and a Hydroshell Hyper or AQ jacket for shorter hikes near Nairobi. The label sewn inside the jacket, or printed on the zip pull, tells you which one you are holding.

Hydroshell is Berghaus's in-house waterproof, breathable membrane. When it launched in 2014, Berghaus split it into three grades and published ratings for each. AQ, and the later AQ2, is the brand's own budget fabric, common on older jackets and school-run coats. Gore-Tex sits at the top of the range.

LabelWaterproof rating (at launch)BreathabilityKenyan use
Hydroshell Elite Pro20,000 mm20,000 g/m²/24hMt Kenya, Kilimanjaro, the Aberdares in the rains
Hydroshell Elite15,000 mm20,000 g/m²/24hHard, sweaty climbs where breathability counts
Hydroshell Hyper15,000 mm10,000 g/m²/24hDay hikes near Nairobi, light packing
Gore-TexVaries by Gore-Tex fabricVariesLong wet days, multi-day treks
AQ / AQ2Not published per jacketLower than HydroshellShort wet outings, town, matatu commutes

A 15,000 mm rating means the fabric held back a 15-metre column of water in a lab test. In practice, both 15,000 and 20,000 mm shells keep out a two-hour storm on Ngong Hills. The higher figure pays off when a heavy pack presses the fabric against your shoulders for six hours on a wet Aberdares track.

Is Berghaus Hydroshell as good as Gore-Tex?

Berghaus Hydroshell is not identical to Gore-Tex, but the Elite grades publish ratings that match many Gore-Tex jackets for Kenyan conditions. Berghaus positioned Hydroshell as a mid-priced alternative, and at launch a Hydroshell Elite Pro jacket cost roughly a fifth less in the UK than a comparable Gore-Tex one.

Where Gore-Tex still has an edge is name recognition and resale value. On a second-hand rail, a Gore-Tex label tells you the jacket was a top-tier model when new, and that usually means better seam taping, stiffer hood peaks and more adjustment points. A Hydroshell Elite jacket is a sensible, cheaper buy if the membrane is still sound.

Is an old Berghaus AQ jacket worth buying?

An old Berghaus AQ or AQ2 jacket is worth buying for short, wet day hikes and everyday use in Nairobi, as long as the seams are intact. It is a weaker choice for Mt Kenya or a full day in the Aberdares, where you need a shell that stays dry for hours under a pack.

Berghaus Jackets, Fleeces and Packs That Suit Kenyan Trails

Three Berghaus families earn their place on Kenyan trails: waterproof shells such as the RG Alpha 2.0, Prism fleeces made with Polartec, and Freeflow daypacks with a ventilated back. Each covers a different job, and together they form a full layering system.

Waterproof shells: the RG Alpha 2.0 as an example

The men's RG Alpha 2.0 is a good example of a current Berghaus walking shell. Berghaus lists it with a Hydroshell fabric, a roll-away adjustable hood, a covered centre zip, two hand-warmer pockets and adjustable cuffs and hem. A size L weighs 598 g and has a 79 cm back length, long enough to cover your hips when you lift your arms to grab a rock on a scramble.

That roll-away hood is a small detail that helps on Kenyan days. You start a Longonot climb in sunshine with the hood tucked away, then pull it out in seconds when a storm rolls over the crater rim in the afternoon. Look for the same features on older Berghaus shells: a stiffened peak, a storm flap or water-resistant zip, and Velcro cuffs that still grip.

Fleeces: the Prism Guide InterActive

Berghaus Prism fleeces use fabric from Polartec, one of the best-known fleece makers. The Prism Guide InterActive weighs 512 g, has four zipped pockets, reinforced chest panels and a stand-up collar. A size L has a 75 cm back length.

The word "InterActive" matters. It means the fleece has a zip and connection points that let it clip inside a compatible Berghaus waterproof, so the two layers move as one jacket on a cold Mt Kenya morning. If you find an InterActive fleece and an InterActive shell on the same rail, buy them together. For more on fleece weights and layering, see our guide to fleece jackets in Nairobi.

Daypacks: the Freeflow back system

The Berghaus Freeflow back system uses a curved frame and a tensioned mesh panel to hold the pack away from your spine. Berghaus says its own testing showed backs stay about 30% drier than with a close-fitting pack. The range has included the Freeflow 25 and 35, with women's versions that have their own back length, harness shape and hip belt.

A sweat-free back is worth a lot on the exposed grassland of Ngong Hills at noon or the open climb up Ol Donyo Sabuk. Freeflow 25 and 35 packs also carry a rain cover, stretch bottle pockets, hydration compatibility and trekking-pole holders. If you cannot find one, our 28L day hiking backpack covers the same day-hike job.

Boots and gaiters

Berghaus also makes walking boots, though fewer reach Kenya than its jackets. The Hillwalker II GTX, for example, pairs a Pittards oiled leather upper with a Gore-Tex Performance Comfort lining, an OrthoLite footbed and a Berghaus Opti-Stud rubber outsole. For a fuller comparison of boot makers, read our guide to hiking boot brands in Kenya.

The Yeti gaiter deserves a mention too. If you spot a pair second-hand, they are excellent for bamboo mud on Elephant Hill or wet moorland grass above Chogoria. A newer, lighter option is a pair of our waterproof leg gaiters.

How Does Berghaus Sizing Run?

Berghaus uses British sizing, which most Kenyan hikers find true to the letter size, with room for a fleece underneath. The most useful number on a spec sheet is the back length, because it tells you whether the jacket covers your lower back on climbs.

Men's jackets come in letter sizes from XS to XXL. Women's pieces are often labelled in UK dress sizes, such as 10, 12 or 14, alongside a letter. Remember that a UK 12 is not the same as a US 12. If a second-hand label only shows a dress size, try it on or measure it against a jacket you already own.

Fit checkWhat good looks likeWhy it matters on Kenyan trails
Arms raised overheadHem stays below your beltRain cannot reach your back on Longonot's scrambles
Fleece underneathZips up without pulling across the chestYou will layer up on Mt Kenya and Kilimanjaro summit nights
Hood up, head turnedPeak turns with your headYou can still see the path in Aberdares fog
CuffsCover the wrist bone with arms outKeeps gloves and sleeves dry when using poles
Pack onHip belt sits over the jacket, not on a zipAvoids rubbing holes in the membrane

Berghaus pages give chest and arm measurements by size. If you are between two sizes and plan to hike Mt Kenya, go one size up so a down jacket fits underneath. For day hikes in the Nairobi area, stick with your usual size so the jacket does not flap in the wind.

Buying Second-Hand Berghaus: What to Check

A second-hand Berghaus jacket is a good buy when the seam tape is flat, the zips run smoothly and the inner membrane has no peeling. Those three checks take two minutes and tell you more than the colour or the price tag ever will.

Thrifted gear is how most Kenyans get into brands like Berghaus without paying new British prices. Our shop sells quality thrifted gear plus some new items, and that mix keeps good kit affordable. The trade-off is that you become the person checking condition, so use this list.

  1. Turn the jacket inside out. On a taped jacket, the seam tape should lie flat. Lifting or bubbling tape lets water in along the seams.
  2. Look at the inner coating. Older two-layer and AQ jackets can have a coating that flakes or feels sticky. If flakes come off on your hand, walk away.
  3. Run every zip end to end. The main zip, pit zips and pocket zips should not catch or split behind the slider.
  4. Check the hood adjusters and hem drawcords. Missing toggles are a cheap fix; a torn drawcord channel is not.
  5. Read the care label. It confirms the fabric (Gore-Tex, Hydroshell or AQ) and often the year range of the model.
  6. Sprinkle a little water on the shoulders. If it beads, the water-repellent finish still works. If it soaks in, plan to re-proof it.
  7. Smell it. A sour smell in the armpits usually washes out, but mildew spots on the lining rarely do.

How can you tell a genuine Berghaus jacket?

A genuine Berghaus jacket usually has neat, even stitching, a sewn-in care label with fabric details, and branded zip pulls or toggles. Counterfeits of big outdoor brands often have blurry logos, a thin "waterproof" fabric that is not taped inside, and care labels with spelling mistakes or no fabric details.

Keep these as general signs rather than proof. Any brand's labels change over the years, and a faded logo on a ten-year-old jacket is normal wear. The fabric and seam tape matter more than the badge: a well-taped jacket keeps you dry whatever the label says.

You will mostly find Berghaus in Nairobi on second-hand outdoor rails, where pieces arrive mixed in with other British and European brands. Stock is unpredictable, so it helps to know what you want before you start looking.

Pro Tips for Berghaus Buyers

  • Read the zip pull: many Berghaus shells print Gore-Tex or Hydroshell there as well as on the inner label.
  • Pair InterActive pieces: an InterActive fleece zips into a compatible Berghaus shell for one warm, dry jacket.
  • Buy for the worst day: choose your shell for summit night or a full Aberdares downpour, not for a sunny Karura walk.
  • Mind the hip belt: try the jacket on with your pack so the belt does not sit on a zip.
  • Re-proof before October: refresh the water-repellent finish before the short rains, and again before the long rains in March.

How Do You Care for a Berghaus Jacket in Kenya?

Wash a Berghaus waterproof at 30°C with a technical cleaner, skip fabric softener, then tumble dry on low or iron cool to reactivate the water-repellent finish. Berghaus's own care labels give these settings and warn against bleach and dry cleaning.

Red murram dust is the hidden enemy here. Dust and sweat clog the pores of a breathable membrane, so a jacket that comes back from Hell's Gate or Ngong Hills caked in fine soil breathes less on the next hike. Rinse or wash it after dusty outings, not only after rain. If you have no tumble drier, a cool iron through a thin cloth does the same job of reviving the finish.

Store the jacket hanging, not stuffed in a bag for months. Nairobi's long rains bring damp air, and a jacket packed away wet in April can grow mildew by June. For a deeper look at fabrics and storage, see our guide to rain jackets for hiking in Nairobi.

When is it time to retire an old Berghaus jacket?

Retire a Berghaus jacket when water comes through the fabric itself even after washing and re-proofing, or when the inner coating flakes. Small tears, missing toggles and tired cuffs can be repaired, but a failed membrane cannot. At that point it still makes a fine windbreaker for dry-season walks.

Building a Kenyan Kit Around Berghaus

A Berghaus shell or fleece works best as one piece of a layered kit, not the whole kit. Match it to the trail: a light shell for day hikes near Nairobi, and a full three-layer system for anything above 3,500 m.

For a wet-season day hike on Ngong Hills or Ol Donyo Sabuk, a Hydroshell Hyper or AQ jacket, a quick-dry T-shirt, light trousers and a daypack are enough. For the Aberdares, add a fleece and Thinsulate waterproof gloves, because rain at 3,500 m feels far colder than rain in town. For Mt Kenya or Kilimanjaro, carry a Gore-Tex or Hydroshell Elite shell, a Polartec fleece, a down or synthetic insulated jacket, thermal base layers, a warm hat and a headlamp. Long rains run roughly from March to May and short rains from October to December, so time a big climb for the drier months and check the Kenya Meteorological Department forecast before you leave.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Berghaus a good brand for hiking?

Berghaus is a well-established hiking brand with roots going back to 1966 and a long record of waterproof jackets, fleeces and rucksacks. Its gear is designed for cold, wet British hills, which makes it a natural fit for Kenya's high mountains. As with any brand, check the fabric label, because a Gore-Tex shell and an old AQ jacket do very different jobs.

Is Berghaus better than The North Face?

Berghaus and The North Face both make capable hiking jackets, and neither is better across the board. Berghaus leans towards practical British walking gear with its own Hydroshell fabric, while The North Face is known for its own membranes and expedition down. Compare the specific jacket's fabric, fit and condition rather than the badge. Our North Face guide covers that brand's lines.

Can I wear a Berghaus jacket on Mt Kenya?

A Berghaus Gore-Tex or Hydroshell Elite jacket works well on Mt Kenya as the outer shell over a fleece and an insulated layer. On summit morning at Point Lenana, 4,985 m, the shell blocks wind and sleet while the layers underneath provide warmth. An older AQ jacket is better kept for lower, shorter hikes than for the summit push.

Do Berghaus jackets run big or small?

Berghaus jackets generally run true to British letter sizes, with enough room in walking shells to wear a fleece underneath. Women's pieces may show UK dress sizes, which differ from US sizes. The safest approach is to compare the back length and chest measurement on the spec sheet, or try the jacket on with your hiking layers.

How do I make an old Berghaus jacket waterproof again?

Restore an old Berghaus jacket by washing it with a technical cleaner at 30°C, then applying a spray-on or wash-in water-repellent treatment and drying it on low heat. Re-proofing revives the outer finish so rain beads off again. It cannot fix peeling seam tape or a flaking inner coating, so check those first.

Final Thoughts

Two minutes with the inner label tells you most of what a Berghaus jacket can do. Gore-Tex and Hydroshell Elite shells are worth buying for Mt Kenya, Kilimanjaro and the Aberdares, while Hyper and AQ pieces suit wetter day hikes around Nairobi. Polartec Prism fleeces and Freeflow daypacks round out the kit.
